releaseClaim.userOperation: A service, desktop app or mobile app submits weighted AI tasks to a pool; the pool never runs more than its capacity in any resource dimension, never silently loses an accepted task across executor panic, shutdown or process crash (Postgres lease queue or embedded store; the pgmq backend provides lease redelivery per S-18 but pool-level crash durability on pgmq is not claimed), and the caller retrieves the result later from the mailbox even after disconnecting. Documented on a branded site with cited theory and compiled examples.
supportedEnvironments: macOS aarch64 and Linux x86_64 (full tests)
Tauri desktop via embedded redb store
Android arm64 and iOS device/simulator (check builds)
releaseClaim.currentCapabilities: As of main@90a6194 (assessment.md): capacity enforced only in ResourcePool; no panic containment; Postgres backends non-functional; JSONL embedded queue not crash-safe; hooks unwired; CI fully red; no docs site.
explicitUnknowns: Throughput/latency figures (benchmarks do not compile today)
pgmq extension build on PG18 inside the project image (unproven until cr-43)
UniFFI async support level for the chosen API surface
Iggy server version to pin for CI
Token/cost budget for a 37-change multi-agent phase

scenarioMatrix.name: Capacity invariant (dispatcher + semaphore model)
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: RUSTFLAGS="--cfg parking_lot_loom" LOOM_MAX_PREEMPTIONS=3 cargo test -p prometheus-parking-lot-core --test loom_capacity --locked
scenarioMatrix.oracle: No explored schedule has sum(active cost) > max_units and no accepted task is lost
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: With --cfg parking_lot_negative_control="s-1" (semaphore acquire skipped) the model reports a violation
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: Pure in-memory; loom with bounded preemptions
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, test names and pass/fail counts from stdout, git SHA, toolchain version

scenarioMatrix.name: No lost wakeup under submit/complete races
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: RUSTFLAGS="--cfg parking_lot_loom" LOOM_MAX_PREEMPTIONS=3 cargo test -p prometheus-parking-lot-core --test loom_wakeup --locked
scenarioMatrix.oracle: Every accepted task is dispatched; no task stays parked while sufficient capacity is free
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: With --cfg parking_lot_negative_control="s-2" (depth check and enqueue under separate locks, as on main@90a6194) the model finds the stranded-task schedule
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, test names and pass/fail counts from stdout, git SHA, toolchain version

scenarioMatrix.name: Executor panic containment (native pools)
scenarioMatrix.oracle: 1 panicking task of 100: 99 complete, capacity returns to 0, stats.failed == 1, panicked status in mailbox
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: With --cfg parking_lot_negative_control="s-3" (catch_unwind skipped) capacity leaks and the test fails
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, test names and pass/fail counts from stdout, git SHA, toolchain version

scenarioMatrix.name: Bounded execution in every pool
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: cargo nextest run -p prometheus-parking-lot-runtime-tokio --locked -E "test(budget_)" && wasm-pack test --headless --chrome crates/parking-lot-wasm
scenarioMatrix.oracle: A never-returning executor is cancelled at its budget; units released; timeout status delivered
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: A cancel witness (Drop fires only on cancellation) does not fire for in-budget tasks; with --cfg parking_lot_negative_control="s-4" (budget not applied) the wedged-executor test fails
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, test names and pass/fail counts from stdout, git SHA, toolchain version

scenarioMatrix.name: Postgres lease redelivery
scenarioMatrix.oracle: A consumer killed with SIGKILL mid-task: task redelivered after lease expiry and completed exactly once
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: With --cfg parking_lot_negative_control="s-5" (lease never expires) no redelivery occurs and the test fails
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: Fresh container per test from tag parking-lot-pg:18 (image digest recorded)
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, test names and pass/fail counts from stdout, git SHA, toolchain version

scenarioMatrix.name: No double claim with concurrent dispatchers
scenarioMatrix.oracle: With 8 dispatchers and 10k tasks, no task is leased by two dispatchers simultaneously
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: With --cfg parking_lot_negative_control="s-6" (SKIP LOCKED/row lock omitted) duplicates are detected
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, test names and pass/fail counts from stdout, git SHA, toolchain version

scenarioMatrix.name: Consume-once mailbox with first-write-wins
scenarioMatrix.oracle: Two consume transactions coordinated by a barrier: exactly one receives the result; duplicate deliveries keep the first write; expired results are evicted
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: With --cfg parking_lot_negative_control="s-7" (SELECT then DELETE in separate statements) the barrier-coordinated test observes double delivery deterministically
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, test names and pass/fail counts from stdout, git SHA, toolchain version

scenarioMatrix.name: Embedded store crash safety
realCollaborators: child process aborted at instrumented points
scenarioMatrix.oracle: After abort at every crash point and restart, each accepted task is present exactly once or redelivered per lease rules
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: With --cfg parking_lot_negative_control="s-8" (enqueue commit skipped) a task is lost and the test fails
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, test names and pass/fail counts from stdout, git SHA, toolchain version

scenarioMatrix.name: No loss on shutdown; requeue across restart
scenarioMatrix.oracle: Every accepted task is completed, captured by the cancellation sink, or requeued; requeued tasks run after restart
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: With --cfg parking_lot_negative_control="s-9" (received task dropped on the shutdown flag) the loss is detected
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, test names and pass/fail counts from stdout, git SHA, toolchain version

scenarioMatrix.name: Notifier failure never loses a stored result
scenarioMatrix.oracle: With a notifier failing every call, every result is stored and consumable
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: With --cfg parking_lot_negative_control="s-10" (notify-before-store, aborting on notifier error) results are lost and the test fails
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, test names and pass/fail counts from stdout, git SHA, toolchain version

scenarioMatrix.name: Iggy events: deterministic IDs and non-blocking publish
scenarioMatrix.oracle: A subscriber receives mailbox.ready per completed task and replays from an earlier offset; publishing the same idempotency key twice yields one message ID; with the server paused, dispatch latency stays within the configured bound
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: With --cfg parking_lot_negative_control="s-11" (random message IDs; synchronous publish) the ID and latency assertions fail
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, test names and pass/fail counts from stdout, git SHA, toolchain version

functionalScope: Unit-weighted (then multi-resource) admission enforced by one dispatcher shared by all pools
Panic containment, bounded execution, async result slots with TTL
Async lease/ack queue, async mailbox and notifier contracts with a conformance suite
Postgres lease queue, Postgres mailbox, pgmq-over-SQL backend, embedded redb queue
Shutdown policy with cancellation capture and durable requeue
Typed configuration building pools and backends
Workspace split with a wasm-safe core; wasm, mobile (UniFFI) and Tauri reach
Branded Docusaurus site with cited theory/history chapters and compiled scenario guides
Versioned 0.3.0 release: changelog, crates.io publication of every workspace crate in dependency order, signed v0.3.0 tag, GitHub release, docs deploy

resilienceScope.policy: Adopted requirements never defer via budget overflow; exhaustion checkpoints and marks BLOCKED. Only never-adopted optional items may defer.

exclusions: Multi-node scheduler coordination (one dispatcher per partition) — later phase
Exactly-once execution (at-least-once + idempotent executors per decision R7)
Flint-specific Postgres extensions from the flint-forge image
Pool-level crash durability on the pgmq backend (lease redelivery only)
Durable dispatch on the web target (no durable backend in the browser)
requiredSafetyChecks: Exposed OpenAI key and Codex tokens rotated by the operator before history purge
History purge only with recorded operator approval; no force-push without it
No agent-tool credentials or runtime state tracked (constraints no-tracked-tool-credentials)
cargo deny advisories clean; gitleaks clean across history
No unsafe code outside generated FFI glue; crate-level deny(unsafe_code) kept in core
Docs sanitizer rejects private paths, secrets and raw wiki content
crates.io publication only after boundary PASS and explicit operator approval, via trusted publishing (no long-lived token in CI)

budgets.tokenFallback: Checkpoint at each milestone; stop and report BLOCKED after two consecutive rounds with no merged change.
budgets.exhaustion: Checkpoint, record BLOCKED with the exhausted dimension, never report PASS; docs and state may be saved without running product tests.

evidenceInvalidation: Evidence is keyed by (scenario id, git SHA of the owning crate, toolchain version, image digest or fixture digest). A change invalidates only evidence whose key it alters; history is preserved and there is no blanket re-review.
